paper text.text: The graph $(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce$ is toroidal exactly when $B+bc$ is planar. If a closed regular neighborhood of $\Psi_3+ce$ in a torus embedding has genus one, its facial walks containing $b,c,d$ have sequences $bcd,bcdc$~\supp{R9}, and both corresponding tests contain $B+bc$. If the neighborhood has genus zero, no boundary walk contains all three attachments, and the only possible annuli meeting all three have sequences $bc\mid ad$ or $bc\mid de$. Their tests are $B+bc+ad$ and $B+bc+de$, each equivalent to planarity of $B+bc$ because the added vertex $a$ or $e$ has degree one. Conversely, choose a plane embedding of $\Psi_3+ce$ with the two facial walks containing $b,c$ and $a,d$ recorded in~\supp{R9}. Remove an open disk from each of these faces and join the two new boundary circles by a cylinder. This gives a torus embedding with an annular face whose attachment sequences are $bc\mid ad$. If $B+bc$ is planar, so is $B+bc+ad$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} places $B$ in this annulus. Contract a $c$--$e$ path whose interior avoids $\Psi_3\cup B$ to $ce$ and keep only $\Psi_3\cup B\cup ce$. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} to a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $B+bc$. The reduction preserves the attachments, connected interior and nonplanarity of $B+bc$, so the resulting minor remains nontoroidal. Minimality and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore give the $563$ forms with added edge $bc$. Every resulting graph has a proper nontoroidal minor except one copy of $\mathfrak T_{41}$, for which $B+bd+cd$ is planar~\supp{E31}, a contradiction. Exchanging $b,e$ and $c,d$ handles $\{c,d,e\}$.

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ...
